source.title: Decoupled Greedy Learning of CNNs
source.authors: Eugene Belilovsky; Michael Eickenberg; Edouard Oyallon

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: The study compares held-out classification performance of decoupled greedy training with backpropagation and other training methods, using test accuracy rather than the claim versions' specific measurements.
record.gate_note: No random-label fitting, width sweep, convolutional-versus-fully-connected comparison, optimizer comparison, dropout intervention, sharpness measurement, or memorized-example removal is reported. Reported results comparing training methods' test accuracy are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: The study measures classification accuracy under different decoupled training methods, auxiliary networks, and asynchronous delays. None of these comparisons tests V1–V8. Using Adam in one experiment and SGD in others is not a controlled optimizer comparison; comparing CNN and MLP auxiliary heads on a shared CNN backbone is not the architecture comparison in V3. The large-batch constraint is mentioned with a citation, without a batch-size experiment.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors present DGL as a strong baseline for parallel CNN training that matches or exceeds competing decoupling approaches and scales to ImageNet. Some experiments show better generalization than backpropagation or sequential greedy training, while accuracy depends on module partition and asynchronous settings.
record.recipe_differences: Uses decoupled greedy local objectives and auxiliary networks rather than joint end-to-end backpropagation; some comparisons use backprop as a reference.
record.method_sensitivity: In asynchronous DGL, test accuracy is maintained through approximately 1.2× layer slowdown, with small losses beyond that; buffer size also changes accuracy, though the reported description is qualitative.

fits_no_version.finding: In the CIFAR-10 DNI reproduction, DGL exceeds DNI and cDNI and generalizes better than backprop with a similar final training loss.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Decoupled greedy CNN training can outperform synthetic-gradient training and standard backpropagation in some settings.

fits_no_version.finding: On the shared CIFAR-10 CNN, CNN-aux, MLP-aux, and MLP-SR-aux achieve accuracies of 92.2, 90.6, and 91.2, with auxiliary FLOP costs of 200%, 0.7%, and 4.0% relative to the largest primary module.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Spatial averaging and smaller auxiliary networks can substantially reduce DGL computation with modest accuracy losses.

fits_no_version.finding: DGL achieves 93.5 ± 0.1 accuracy across three CIFAR-10 trials, alongside reference values of 93.53 for backprop and 93.41 for DDG.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Two-module DGL can match reference backprop and DDG accuracy on ResNet-110 while enabling update unlocking.

fits_no_version.finding: ImageNet DGL top-1 accuracy is comparable to or higher than backprop in several module configurations, but lower for VGG-19 with four modules and VGG-13 trained per layer.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: DGL can retain ImageNet classification accuracy while enabling parallel training, with accuracy depending on architecture and module partition.

fits_no_version.finding: Asynchronous DGL retains synchronous accuracy through approximately 1.2× module slowdown, with small losses beyond that; small replay buffers also cause only slight losses.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Asynchronous DGL with replay tolerates moderate module delays and small replay buffers.

record.code_released: not stated; code for experiments is included in the submission and supplementary materials
record.problems: No random-label or memorization-capacity check is reported. Figure-only results lack numeric values in the text. The paper notes that reproduced DNI accuracy was worse than prior reported results, possibly due to minor implementation differences. The paper says accuracies are the same across backprop, DDG, and DGL, although Table 2 lists 93.53, 93.41, and 93.5 ± 0.1 respectively.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant reported held-out accuracy comparisons were omitted. Training-loss curves and layer-loss curves are not held-out performance measures; wall-clock speed and FLOP counts do not measure generalization.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-versus-random-label held-out performance under the same architecture and recipe.
Width sweeps beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers, including the contribution of local connectivity or initialization.
Controlled adaptive-optimizer versus SGD comparisons and tuning-dependent differences in held-out performance.
Large versus small minibatches under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations that change the penalty.
Dropout interventions, small-data regimes, excessive dropout, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps relative to alternative measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's tests/T2 classification should be changed: generalization performance alone does not test these eight specific claims. All rows concern the study's own training method or its comparators and ablations. No version-specific verdict or missing result is warranted.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test fitting random labels or compare held-out accuracy on natural versus random labels.
Does not sweep network width around the zero-training-error threshold.
Does not compare convolutional and fully connected architectures.
Does not compare adaptive optimizers with SGD or momentum SGD.
Does not vary batch size or compare large and small batches under fixed epoch budgets.
Does not add or remove dropout or weight decay.
Does not measure sharpness or relate it to a train-test gap.
Does not remove memorized examples and retrain.
